findings.reason: Confirmed (high). Corollary 6.8 (arXiv:2102.00372v1, p. 22, page image checked) defines θ(π) only when Θ_J(π) ≠ 0, yet states 'θ(π₁) ≅ θ(π₂) ⟹ π₁ ≅ π₂' for all tempered non-generic π₁, π₂. Its proof makes θ_J(π) the cosocle, which can be 0, and ends 'by Proposition 6.6', which needs π to be a quotient of a nonzero Θ_J(τ). Item cor-6-8 copies the unrestricted implication. The counterexample is correct. For a nontrivial unramified cubic character χ₀ of F×, χ = χ₀ ∘ Nrd is a nontrivial character of PD× (Nrd(z) = z³ on F×). Proposition 7.1(i),(iii) (p. 23) gives Θ(1) = π_deg[1], a nongeneric discrete series (Proposition 3.1(iii), p. 9), and Θ(χ) = π_sc[χ], a nongeneric depth-zero supercuspidal (7.1(ii)). Both are tempered and nongeneric, and they are not isomorphic. By the dichotomy, Theorem 6.1 (p. 19), each has zero lift to PGSp₆, so for J = H₃(M₂(F)) both sides of the implication are 0 while π₁ ≇ π₂. The fix is right: require 0 ≠ θ_J(π₁) ≅ θ_J(π₂) with J fixed, add an arXiv-v1 source issue with the counterexample (the published version was not read), and propagate the hypothesis to the report and route 1's brief.

Confirmed (high). Lemma 11.4 (p. 36, page image checked) states ℓ′(v) = ∫_{Y/X∩Y} ℓ(π(y)v) dy, while its proof's intertwiner Ind_X^H ψ_X ≅ Ind_Y^H ψ_Y is f′(h) = ∫_{Y/X∩Y} f(yh) ψ̄_Y(y) dy, with the character. I checked the Heisenberg counterexample by hand. The action [π(x,y,z)f](t) = ψ(z + yt) f(t + x) is a representation for the law (x,y,z)(x′,y′,z′) = (x+x′, y+y′, z+z′+xy′). X = {(0,y,z)} and Y = {(x,0,z)} are maximal abelian with X ∩ Y the centre. ℓ(f) = f(0) lies in Hom_X(π, ψ_X) for ψ_X(0,y,z) = ψ(z). With ψ_Y(x,0,z) = ψ(z + x) and representatives (x,0,0), the stated ℓ′ is f ↦ ∫ f(x) dx, which is invariant under π(x₀,0,0) instead of transforming by ψ(x₀). Moving a representative by the centre multiplies the unweighted integrand by ψ(z), so ℓ′ is not even defined on the quotient. With the weight ψ_Y(y)⁻¹ both defects vanish: ∫ ψ(−x) f(x + x₀) dx = ψ(x₀) ∫ ψ(−x) f(x) dx. The fix is right: insert ψ_Y(y)⁻¹, record the statement/proof discrepancy as an arXiv-v1 source issue, and keep any unweighted use limited to representatives on which ψ_Y is trivial.

Confirmed (high). The review-added item rev-langlands-classification-and-harish-chandra quantifies over every connected reductive G with ν in the open positive chamber of a_M*, and concludes 'π is tempered iff P = G'. When P = G there are no roots in Δ(P), so ν ranges over all of a_G* = R ⊗ X*(G). I checked the counterexample directly: for G = GL₁, σ = 1 and ν with q^{⟨ν, H(·)⟩} = |·|_F, J(G, 1, ν) = |·|_F is irreducible with P = G, but its value at a uniformizer has absolute value q⁻¹, so it is not unitary and hence not tempered. I did not need the cited Silberger–Zink or Bernstein texts, since the counterexample uses only the item's own quantification. Gan–Savin's §3.4 (p. 12) uses the classification only for G₂, whose centre is trivial, so this is an error in the review's generalization, not in the paper, and belongs in no errata of the paper. The fix is right: tempered iff P = G and ν = 0 (equivalently σ tempered and no positive real central twist), or keep 'iff P = G' only under a unitary-central-character or anisotropic-centre assumption, and update the SR.3 route and the report.
